plan: Given my private value of $6, I want to bid strategically to maximize profit. Since the value is relatively low, I should avoid overbidding and risking a loss. I'll place a conservative bid slightly above half of my value to increase my chances of winning without incurring unnecessary costs. Assuming others might bid higher due to higher values, bidding $3.1 will limit potential losses and is unlikely to win, preserving my profit.

My value for the item is $40. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly above the average expected value of other bids, which is around $24.5. However, since I only pay the third-highest bid, I can afford to bid slightly higher to increase my chances of winning. I will bid $30. This balances the risk of overbidding with the potential profit if I win.

Given my value of $28, I aim to bid just below my value to maximize profit if I win. I assume opponents bid between $20-$30 based on random values. To win, I should bid slightly above average, around $25. This ensures if I win, I pay a lower third-highest bid, maximizing profit.
